chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan and Muhammad, the sons of Ali ibn Yousuf, narrated to us, from their father, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi, from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Abu al-Jarood, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:
When the allegiance (bay'ah) of the young boy appears, every person with a distinctive mark (or claim) will rise with their distinctive mark.

key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: The young boy (referring to the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What happens when the allegiance of the young boy appears according to the signs of the Mahdi?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani highlights a specific eschatological sign where the public recognition of the young Mahdi triggers a surge of competing claimants, each asserting their own legitimacy. In Shia scholarly tradition, this reflects the historical pattern of 'Sufyani-like' uprisings and false messiahs that emerge during the period of anticipation, emphasizing the need for discernment among the faithful. The phrase 'each with his own claim' underscores the fragmentation of political and religious authority preceding the final establishment of justice.
